**Preparation** — `pwd` confirmed repo root; ran `./b4w.ps1 help`, read `SKILL.md` fully plus `references/swarm.md`, `x-sql-dom-load-select.md`, `x-sql-dom-select-functions.md` for exact function signatures. **Commands used (in order):**
```
./b4w.ps1 help                                       # overview + category map
./b4w.ps1 help swarm / --help swarm create / --help swarm query
```

assessment.mostConfusingAspects: The batch-window header and the task rows in the same `swarm list` output use different time bases (UTC vs local, 8 hours apart here), which makes the output look internally inconsistent at first glance. The 'Batch <id>: 10 of 11 tracked swarm task(s)' header reads like a selection/failure count. DURATION values of 5-38 ms for page-scraping tasks contradict the ~1-minute wall clock of the batch, leaving users unsure what the column measures. There is also no visible queue-time metric despite the documented ~30-60 s cold start of a fresh swarm session.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Make all timestamps in swarm list (and across swarm status) use one consistent, zone-labeled time base. 2) Surface queue wait / time-to-result per task (a WAITED or ELAPSED column) so DURATION is not misread. 3) Clarify batch/status filter header wording. 4) Document the non-TTY swarm create auto-clean behavior. Everything else — command discovery via help, seed-file comment handling, batch ids, status/result polling, and resource cleanup — worked exactly as documented and needed no improvement.

issues.title: swarm list prints the batch window in UTC while task rows are local time — 8-hour offset within a single output

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 swarm list   (on any machine whose timezone is not UTC; here UTC+8)
Compare the 'Batch window:' header with the STARTED/FINISHED columns of the table rows.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Every timestamp in one command's output uses the same time base (ideally local time with a date/zone suffix), so the window and the rows can be compared directly.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The header shows 'Batch window: 17:12:05 -> 17:13:09' while the same tasks' rows show '2026-10-14 01:12:05' / '01:13:09' — the same instants rendered 8 hours apart. `swarm list --json` confirms the mapping: started_at 2026-10-13T17:12:06.729Z corresponds to the 01:12:06 row. `swarm status` additionally prints UTC ISO strings (lastModifiedTime ...Z), so the command family mixes two conventions.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Two formatting paths that never agree outside UTC: the batch window is formatted straight from chrono::DateTime<Utc> with .format("%H:%M:%S") (cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs, batch-summary block around lines 15155-15163), while per-task rows are converted with .with_timezone(&chrono::Local) inside summarize_async_tasks (cli/browser4-cli/src/state.rs:1548 and :1566). On a whole-hour offset the minute/second values still look self-consistent, which makes the mismatch easy to miss and easy to misread as a window from a different day/batch.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:15155-15163 (batch window formatting in the swarm list handler); compare cli/browser4-cli/src/state.rs:1497 summarize_async_tasks (rows, uses chrono::Local)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Convert the batch-window instants with .with_timezone(&chrono::Local) before formatting, or route both the header and rows through one shared timestamp formatter
- Include the date and an explicit zone marker in the header (e.g. 'Batch window (local): 2026-10-14 01:12:05 -> 01:13:09')
- Add a regression test that asserts the header and the first/last row render the same clock time under a non-UTC TZ
- Decide the convention for `swarm status` too (it emits UTC 'Z' timestamps) and document it, so users correlating with external logs are not surprised
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: DURATION column understates task time-to-result by ~3 orders of magnitude — queue wait is invisible

sections.body:
1. Submit a batch: ./b4w.ps1 swarm query --sql @q.sql --seed-file seeds.txt
2. Poll until done, then compare `./b4w.ps1 swarm list` with `./b4w.ps1 swarm list --json`.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The DURATION column either reflects how long each job actually took (submit to result), or the output makes it explicit that only worker-processing time is counted.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Task 71eb6240 was submitted at 17:11:51.862Z and completed at 17:12:06.740Z (~15 s to result), but the table shows DURATION 10ms; the whole 10-URL batch spanned 1m03s while row durations are 5-38ms. A page-scraping job completing in 10 ms is implausible if a browser context loaded the page, so either the metric timestamps only a late pipeline phase or a non-browser fetch path served the pages; the table gives no way to tell queue time from work time.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: duration_ms is computed strictly as started_at -> completed_at (as documented in swarm.md), excluding queue wait; the table has no column for submitted->completed elapsed even though --json carries submitted_at. Whether started_at is stamped when real processing begins (vs just before completion) requires backend instrumentation in the browser4-swarm task runner to confirm.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/state.rs:1497 summarize_async_tasks (DURATION column); backend timing lives in the browser4-swarm plugin task runner
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a WAITED/QUEUED column (submitted_at to started_at) or an ELAPSED column (submitted_at to completed_at) so time-to-result is visible without --json
- If the processing window is intentionally only the fetch/parse phase, label the column accordingly (e.g. PROCESS) and state in `--help swarm list` that queue time is excluded
- Verify server-side what started_at actually marks; if it is stamped immediately before completion, fix the instrumentation so the metric reflects real processing duration
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: swarm list --batch header reads as a mismatch: 'Batch <id>: 10 of 11 tracked swarm task(s)'

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 swarm list --batch 879773d4-c6bf-47e5-a6eb-11272a77d3b0   (with at least one other tracked task, e.g. a swarm-submit job, present)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The header states plainly how many tasks the batch contains and how many exist overall, e.g. 'Batch <id>: 10 task(s) (11 tracked in total)'.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: It prints 'Batch 879773d4-...: 10 of 11 tracked swarm task(s)', which reads like 10 of 11 selected/failed; the 11th row actually belongs to a different batch (the plain scrape job). The same 'N of M tracked' pattern appears on the lifecycle-filter line. Additionally, the unfiltered list still labels its summary 'Batch window' even when the visible tasks span several batches, where 'Batch' is ambiguous.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The label is built as '{filtered.len()} of {before} tracked swarm task(s)', where `before` is the count of ALL tracked tasks captured before the batch filter is applied — cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:15098 (same pattern at 15116 for the status filter); the window label is at 15158.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:15098 (batch filter header), :15116 (status filter header), :15158 (batch window label)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Reword to 'Batch <id>: N task(s) (M tracked in total)'
- Print the batch header only when --batch is given; when listing everything, label the summary 'Tracked window' or 'Submission window'
- Apply the same wording fix to the lifecycle-filter line

issues.title: swarm create silently auto-cleans completed tasks from prior sessions in non-TTY runs; the documented prompt/--clear-stale model doesn't cover it

sections.body:
1. Have completed swarm tasks tracked from a prior session (visible in ./b4w.ps1 swarm list).
2. From a non-TTY context (script, CI, piped shell), run: ./b4w.ps1 swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS
3. Observe 'Auto-cleaned 3 completed swarm task(s) from prior sessions.' and the prior tasks disappearing from swarm list.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Per skills/browser4-cli/references/swarm.md, swarm create warns/prompts in a TTY and --clear-stale is the mechanism 'for non-interactive/scripted use'; the non-TTY behavior (auto-clean without the flag) should be documented so scripts relying on retained tracking are not surprised.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Without --clear-stale and with stdin not a TTY, the CLI removed the prior completed tasks' tracking entries automatically (one informational line, no prompt, exit 0). The docs describe only the interactive prompt, implying non-interactive runs without --clear-stale keep the old tasks.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The non-TTY code path of swarm create auto-clears completed tasks instead of prompting or skipping; swarm.md's 'List Tracked Tasks' tip (and the --help swarm create notes) were not updated for this behavior. Which lifecycle states are eligible (completed only, or failed/queued too) was not determined in this run.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (swarm create handling / stale-task clearing); skills/browser4-cli/references/swarm.md ('List Tracked Tasks' tip) and --help swarm create notes (cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Document the non-TTY auto-clean behavior in swarm.md and in the swarm create notes
- State exactly which tasks are auto-cleaned (completed only vs failed/queued as well)
- If retention matters for scripts, offer a --keep/--no-clean flag or print the cleaned task ids so they can be reviewed
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
